Not a defect. Spec section 8 requires secure determinism, not an externally injected nonce. ed25519 already satisfies it: RFC 8032 derives k from the expanded secret key and the message, so Ed25519::sign_deterministic correctly ignores the nonce argument. sr25519 has no such native guarantee, so classical/sr25519.rs implements the spec literally via SeededRng seeded from H(sk || nonce || msg). Both components meet the requirement as written. Confirmed by the maintainer 2026-08-10.

Not a defect. Burning a leaf on every signing attempt is the intended design, not an upstream bug: a signing path that can return without advancing the counter is a leaf-reuse hazard, and reuse is total security failure while a burned leaf is only availability loss. Upstream sign_stateful_action is therefore correct. Our own precheck-before-commit ordering is what is wrong; tracked separately. Confirmed by the maintainer 2026-08-10.

Implemented in 4186e74: sign_stateful commits the leaf before attempting the component signature and validates nothing beforehand; precheck retained for the stateless path and verify; trait docs rewritten; driver test inverted and mutation-checked.

Defence in depth, verified from both sides.

Commit f833961. Budget keyed to a BudgetKey derived from pkSeed||hypertreeRoot alone. The module has no reset operation at all, which makes the audit finding unreachable rather than merely tested against: material change yields a different key and starts a fresh count; unchanged material yields the same key and preserves it, whatever the RotationKind label says. STATELESS_BUDGET sits on the trait, cfg'd 2^20 / 2^18 per profile, and budget.rs takes it as a parameter so the generic module stays independent of the component. Verified independently: rewriting stateless_key_material to return the commitment -- the exact audit finding -- fails stateless_key_material_is_pk_seed_concatenated_with_hypertree_root. The implementer went idle without reporting or committing; the controller verified and committed the work.

Commit e041a81. Exposes only H1 through H4; H5 and H6 throw a JavaScript Error naming the omission, because a JS object holding a stateful secret key can be structured-cloned, serialized, or passed through a MessageChannel, any of which forks the one-time leaf counter. Tested (stateless_suite("H5") and ("H6") both error). Idiomatic JS surface: throws Errors rather than returning codes, Uint8Array in and out, .d.ts checked in and diff-tested, wasm-pack web and nodejs targets, plus a wasm-npm CI job. Honestly documents that the caller's JS-side Uint8Array copy of a secret key cannot be zeroized from Rust.

Open cross-binding item: its error message directs users to the C ABI or Python binding for H5/H6. That claim needs re-checking once those two land -- if Python reaches the same conclusion under the same constraint, the message is wrong and must be corrected.

Commit a5245cf. All six suites exposed. The stateful secret key refuses __copy__, __deepcopy__ and __reduce__ with a dedicated StatefulKeyNotCloneableError whose message names the deliberate alternative (export() plus load_stateful_secret_key(), with the leaf budgets tracked as one) rather than just refusing. Each refusal has a test; 30/30 pytest passed against a maturin-built extension. Per-error-class exception types, not one catch-all. Known limit, documented in src/bytes_in.rs rather than hidden: abi3-py39 cannot reach CPython's buffer-protocol C API below 3.11, so input is bytes/bytearray only, not arbitrary buffer objects.

Resolves the cross-binding item raised on pqhs-civ.3: Python does expose H5/H6, so the wasm binding's error message directing users here is correct.

It is a regression detector rather than a liveness check. It generates a real 128s key from the fixture master seed and asserts the public key equals the pinned fixture bytes, which covers the whole 2^18 hypertree root derivation.
